title: Jefferson County justices retain attorney amid malfeasance lawsuit - NewsBreak
text: PINE BLUFF, Ark . — Seven Jefferson County Justices of the Peace held a special quorum court meeting Wednesday to retain legal counsel in response to a civil lawsuit that accuses them of malfeasance and calls for their removal from office. The suit, filed by five county residents, alleges the justices acted unlawfully by holding meetings without proper procedure, attempting to pass ordinances, and voting to use county funds to pay for legal expenses—all without the required approval from County Judge Gerald Robinson. District 3 Justice Reginald Johnson said the justices are caught in a legal bind. “The justices have been confronted with lawsuits and basically our hands are tied behind our backs,” Johnson said. “We try to get representation, the judge will not sign for us to have representation. That’s basically being in the fight with no hands.” With the legal dispute escalating, the justices voted during the special meeting to retain Benton attorney Bobby McCallister to represent them moving forward. “The best part of working with this group is I wanted to make sure that we had a commitment to do things the right way—that we are going to be transparent,” McCallister said. “The goal is to just let these guys get back to legislating for this county.” District 11 Justice Richard “Doc” Victorino echoed the need for legal support following the initial filing back in April being dismissed, and now just a few days ago being reopened. “Now that it’s come back to life, professional representation is warranted,” he said. According to court documents, the justices are accused of attempting to pass a $31,261.82 claim to pay their previous legal bills without the county judge’s approval, despite being legally prohibited from authorizing such payments. Jefferson County Chief Deputy Prosecutor Karres Manning Center said the justices may act if they follow state law. “If you have followed the correct procedures and take the vote forward, then you are within your right, yes,” she said. The plaintiffs in the case are asking the court to remove the justices from office and award damages, including attorneys’ fees. The full lawsuit can be read here .
